steps.title: Derive the nonnegative residual and gradient growth
steps.text: Hessian0..L produces convexity and L-Lipschitz gradient through the canonical curvature provider. The normalized stationary origin then yields rho>=0 and gradientnorm<=Lnormu. No extra convexity or growth premise is introduced; L0 and dimension0 are included.

steps.title: Normalize against the actual standard Gaussian
steps.text: The real exponential is positive and bounded by1. Gaussian probability gives its L1 and strictly positive finite integral Z<=1. The literal tilt is exactly withDensity(exp(-rho)/Z), integrates to1 and is a genuine probability.
steps.formula: \gamma=\mathcal N(0,I),\quad Z=\int e^{-\rho}d\gamma\in(0,1],\quad q=e^{-\rho}/Z,\quad r=q\gamma,\quad\int q\,d\gamma=1.

steps.title: Identify the canonical volume Gibbs law
steps.text: Use the compiled covariance-identity Gaussian density against canonical volume. Its actual mass1 forces the ordinary quadratic partition to be finite and positive; normalize that exact density. Consecutive tilts then identify the Gaussian-relative residual law with the volume Gibbs potential norm²/2+rho.

steps.title: Differentiate the explicit positive square root
steps.text: The everywhere chosen f=exp(-rho/2)/sqrtZ is C2, strictly positive and satisfies f²=q. Ordinary Frechet chain rules and the Hilbert Riesz identification yield its gradient and the log-density gradient. No arbitrary pointwise RN representative is differentiated.

steps.title: Produce the finite gradient and entropy domains
steps.text: The actual Gaussian second moment dominates exp(-rho)normgradρ² by L²normu². This gives gradρ L2r and gradf L2gamma after multiplying by the proved normalizer. f L2 follows from q L1. The bound rho exp(-rho)<=1 and logq=-rho-logZ give entropy L1 without assuming its finiteness.
steps.formula: e^{-\rho}\|\nabla\rho\|^2\le L^2\|u\|^2,\quad\int\|u\|^2d\gamma=d,\quad0\le\rho e^{-\rho}\le1,\quad q\log q=-Z^{-1}\rho e^{-\rho}-q\log Z.

steps.title: Integrate the exact Dirichlet-Fisher identity
steps.text: Integrate normgradf²=(1/4)qnormgradρ² against gamma and rewrite the actual tilted integral. The domains have already been proved, so both energies are finite. This is the Euclidean Hilbert energy with the exact factor1/4; no LSI or transport inequality is asserted.
